MatrixNet BPNN (batch forward/backprop, optional BATCH_PROP rprop speeds, early-stop on validation EMA, dropout) trains to predict next-bar EMA increment; indicator can roll the 1-step forecast into _futBars multi-step.

mechanism: TradeNN EA concatenates Depth bars of tick-value-normalized close increments across Symbols (default XAGUSD,XAUUSD,EURUSD) into one input row; Diff() accumulates past increments /sqrt(lag) as RW-normalized features; target is next traded-symbol increment; MatrixNet (5 layers, HiddenLayerFactor, DropOutPercentage) trains then signs the feed-forward output for BUY/SELL. Models saved via MatrixNetStore with 3σ scale.

mechanism: Modified Spiral Dynamics Optimization (SDOm): per-coordinate damped harmonic oscillator x(t)=A·e^(-γt)·cos(ωt+φ) around global best; amplitude reset on new optimum; best particle randomly rethrown. Ranked on Rastrigin/Forest/Megacity AO stand—parameter search, not market sensing.

mechanism: Across a synchronized symbol basket (28 forex majors or custom), compute per-symbol Relative Strength from offensive/defensive scores vs median benchmark return over rs_period. RS spread = mean(top−bottom) RS for rs_percent_top fraction. Rising/wide spread = positive-feedback expansion (trend regime); narrow/converging spread = negative-feedback contraction (range/choppy).
data_needed: Synced OHLCV for index members; ENUM_PRICE (close/median/typical/weighted); DIFF_LOG or DIFF_PERCENT returns; rs_period; rs_percent_top.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: INDEX_FOREX_MAJORS (~28 pairs) or custom list; PERIOD_CURRENT; example AppliedPeriod 7–25; MaxBars ~300
why_new_for_mis: Cross-sectional RS dispersion is a basket-level regime sensor distinguishing trend-friendly positive feedback from choppy negative feedback without single-symbol indicators.
quote: When the markets are gripped by positive feedback the weakest and strongest securities diverge depending on the direction of the trend. … If prices are stuck in a range there is relatively little difference between the weakest and strongest securities, there is convergence.

mechanism: Partition rs_period benchmark returns about their median into offensive (≥median) and defensive (<median) sums of (r−median). For each symbol, sum its returns on those same bars and express as % of the matching benchmark offense/defense total. Scatter of (defense,offense) expands in positive feedback and contracts in negative feedback.
data_needed: Same basket returns; rs_period window; MathMedian of benchmark returns.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex majors basket; PERIOD_CURRENT; AppliedPeriod e.g. 25; MaxBars animation example 50
why_new_for_mis: Splits relative performance into trend-participation vs drawdown-resilience axes—MIS can score symbols by regime-conditioned offense/defense rather than raw return.
quote: The offensive score is the performance achieved when benchmark returns are above average. The defensive score is calculated similarly using the returns achieved when benchmark returns are less than average.

mechanism: Average returns of top/bottom rs_percent_top RS names over lag window → RS leaders and laggards. Combine with RS-spread trend: rising spread + rising leaders → buy strongest; rising spread + rising laggards → short weakest; negative-feedback (contracted spread) → stay out as risk filter.
data_needed: Per-bar RS ranks; rs_percent_top; leader/laggard return averages; RS spread series.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Forex majors index; PERIOD_CURRENT; rs_period and rs_percent_top inputs
why_new_for_mis: Turns Janus dialectics into an actionable regime-change gate: when feedback polarity flips, MIS can switch between leader-long, laggard-short, or flat.
quote: When the trend of the spread is rising in combination with the rs leaders it is an indication of positive feedback along with net buying of strong performers. … Another option is to use the spread indicator, as a filter for risk. When there is positive feedback the market is less risky, with negative feedback being an indicator of possible choppy conditions.

mechanism: CArima fits ARIMA(p,d,q) (optional non-contiguous AR/MA lags, optional constant) by differencing series d times, recursively building innovation, minimizing prediction SSE via Powell's method; coefficients retrieved for forecast; integrate back to original domain.

mechanism: Interpret ACF/PACF: if PACF cuts off after lag p while ACF decays → pure AR(p); if ACF cuts off after lag q while PACF decays → pure MA(q). Use cutoffs (plus AIC/BIC/grid/CV) to choose (p,q) and d via differencing-to-stationarity before Fit().
data_needed: Autocorrelation and partial autocorrelation of the (differenced) series over candidate lags.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Hypothetical AR(1)/MA(1) sign examples; general time series including FX after differencing
why_new_for_mis: Turns ACF/PACF morphology into an explicit order/regime diagnostic that tells MIS whether a series is AR-like, MA-like, or needs more differencing before forecasting.
quote: In general if partial autocorrelations cut off beyond a certain lag and the autocorrelations simultaneously begin to decay beyond the same lag then the series can be modeled by a pure AR model up to the observed cut off lag on the partial autocorrelation plot.
